feedback.problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+6\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+109y=0.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $y={e}^{\lambda x}.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}+6\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+109{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +109) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +109=0.
$$

The auxiliary equation can be solved by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +109 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +9)-9+109 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2}+100 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2} & =-100 \\ \lambda +3 & =\pm 10\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-3\pm 10\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={e}^{-3x}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡10x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡10x).\end{aligned}
$$
